stories.title: Fed's Goolsbee Says Inflation Is Moving the Wrong Way as Hike Bets Firm

photo.alt: The Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago building with a U.S. flag; file photo.

paragraphs: Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee said Friday the central bank has work to do to restore its credibility on inflation. He told CNBC inflation is rising and starting to spread. He spoke after new wholesale price data.

The producer price index rose 0.3% in October, slightly below forecasts. CNBC reports it was up 6.5% from a year earlier, the biggest annual gain since November 2022. The 10-year Treasury yield rose to about 5.14%.
Goolsbee pointed to demand from the AI data center buildout as a new source of pressure. He said the Fed is not on a path back to its 2% target. He is not a voter on rates this year.

Why it matters. Higher rates raise costs for mortgages, car loans and credit cards. Traders now price a 100% chance of a hike at the Dec. 9 meeting, according to CME Group's FedWatch. CNBC puts the odds of a half-point move at about 14%.

stories.title: Duffy Seeks $50 Billion After Aging Air Traffic Gear Halts US Flights

photo.alt: Departure boards above empty check-in desks at a Spanish airport; file photo.

paragraphs: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy is asking Congress for about $50 billion after old equipment forced a nationwide halt to departures Friday. BBC News reports it was the longest nationwide ground stop since the Sept. 11 attacks. It lasted more than four hours.

Duffy said airspace reopened at 8:15 p.m. ET. The Guardian reports more than 11,000 U.S. flights were delayed or canceled, citing FlightAware. More than 3,500 planes were in the air when the order came.

Duffy said overloaded routers in an old system gave inconsistent data, so officials shut it down. Al Jazeera reports officials said new technology added to the system overloaded older parts. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said there was no sign of a cyberattack.

Why it matters. Duffy warned the old system is going to continue to fail. NBC News reports he expects operations to recover before the Thanksgiving travel rush. Duffy said the effects could ripple for a few days.

stories.title: Bessent Says Agencies Sought Curbs on a Firm Tied to the Nvidia Scandal

photo.alt: Close-up of a dark blue printed circuit board; illustrative file photo.

paragraphs: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Friday that several agencies wanted export curbs on Megaspeed for months. He told CNBC the Commerce Department is in charge of that decision. Megaspeed is at the center of the scandal that ended Jensen Huang's run as Nvidia chief.

Bessent said Treasury, Defense, State and the trade representative's office all backed adding Megaspeed to the entity list. He said leakage of advanced chips to China hurts U.S. companies. Commerce had earlier denied a reported clash between Bessent and Secretary Howard Lutnick.

Bessent said the real question is whether Nvidia knew its client. NBC News reports U.S. officials said the Nvidia case should have no bearing on Trump's coming China trip. They said export controls are not up for negotiation.

Why it matters. The dispute exposes a rift inside the administration over chip policy. Lutnick and Huang have been asked to testify before the Senate Banking Committee next month. Commerce did not respond to CNBC about Bessent's remarks.

stories.title: Qatar and Turkiye Sign a Mutual Defense Pact as Gulf Tensions Persist

photo.alt: A ferry crosses the Bosphorus below mosques in Istanbul; file photo.

paragraphs: Qatar and Turkiye have agreed to a mutual defense pact against any outside armed attack on either country. Al Jazeera reports it followed a meeting in Istanbul on Friday. Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and Qatar's emir chaired the talks.

The two countries will consult on threats and expand joint drills, arms production and training. The joint communique did not say what would trigger the pact or how they would respond. An analyst at Qatar University said it is meant to deter, not to target a country.
The deal comes as the region deals with fallout from the U.S. and Israeli war on Iran. Al Jazeera's live coverage reports Iran says five tankers caught fire near Hormuz in 24 hours.

Why it matters. Gulf states are seeking new security ties and less reliance on outside powers. Ankara and Doha called for the swift and full reopening of safe passage through the Strait of Hormuz. Analysts expect cooperation on drones and air defense.

deep_dive.title: What to Expect When Trump, Xi and Putin Meet in Shenzhen

photo.alt: Shenzhen's Houhai skyline reflected in the bay at dusk; file photo.

paragraphs: President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin plan a first three-way meeting next week. NBC News reports it will take place on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen. The White House announced it Friday night.

What happened. A White House spokesperson said Trump will discuss reducing nuclear weapons. A senior U.S. official said no agreement is expected and called it a first conversation. Trump also plans to raise the Iran war. Officials said Ukraine is on a separate track and will not be discussed.

The backstory. Al Jazeera reports the last U.S. and Russian nuclear arms treaty, New START, expired in February. Trump then sought a new deal that includes China. NBC News cites Pentagon estimates that China has more than 600 warheads. The U.S. and Russia each have more than 5,000.

What comes next. The Guardian reports Ukraine fears a Yalta-style carve-up of influence by the three powers. Al Jazeera reports the Kremlin dismissed that comparison but called the meeting extremely significant. The Guardian reports China is already trying to push nuclear disarmament off the agenda. NBC News reports no separate one-on-one meeting with Putin is scheduled. Elon Musk will travel with Trump but skip the official meetings.

trivia.explanation: C. 6.5%. CNBC reports it was the biggest annual gain since November 2022.

poll.question: Should the Fed raise interest rates at its December meeting?

World view: Siege deepens disease fears in Taiz. Health officials logged 5,642 disease cases in four weeks as a Houthi siege cuts off supplies; Al Jazeera reports.
Winter strains Gaza shelters. UNICEF says winter supplies are arriving but far short of needs after floods hit 220,000 people; Al Jazeera reports.
Need to know: Alaska picks its youngest governor. Democrat Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins, 37, flips the office from Republicans in a projected win; NBC News reports.
Hassett denies he is leaving. The National Economic Council director called a report of his planned exit not true; CNBC reports.
Money & markets: Apple hits a record high. Shares reached an intraday record of $360.80 on Friday as investors moved away from AI infrastructure names; CNBC reports.
Chip rivals rally on Nvidia turmoil. AMD and Broadcom are up about 17% over the past week, and Nvidia reports earnings Nov. 17; CNBC reports.
Future frontiers: Starship booster catch called off. SpaceX diverted its Super Heavy booster to the ocean on Friday while the upper stage kept flying; BBC News reports.
A blood test speeds cancer matching. A Manchester lab cut results for a gene test that guides targeted lung and breast cancer drugs to 14 days; BBC News reports.
The score: Pochettino leaves the U.S. team. The coach became Manchester United's head coach and will lead the U.S. against Haiti on Nov. 14 and 18 first; BBC Sport reports.
Indiana hosts USC. The ninth-ranked defending champion Hoosiers face No. 18 USC on Saturday with playoff stakes on the line; CBS Sports reports.
Life & culture: A new Bond draws near. Amazon MGM Studios is preparing to name the next 007, with five actors widely seen as the shortlist; The Guardian reports.
Darth Vader's lightsaber sells for $4.875 million. The prop from The Empire Strikes Back set a record for an on-screen Star Wars item; The Guardian reports.

stories.title: Supreme Court Agrees to Weigh Trump's Asylum Ban at the Southern Border

photo.alt: The U.S. Supreme Court building; file photo, 2024.

paragraphs: The Supreme Court agreed Friday to consider President Trump's ban on asylum at the southern border. AP reports lower courts found it illegal to block asylum applications. The order called the border situation an "invasion." Arguments are expected in spring, with a ruling by the end of June.

Reuters reports a federal judge ruled against the policy in July 2025, and an appeals court upheld that ruling in April. Solicitor General D. John Sauer wrote that border encounters have fallen 93% since the order took effect. Immigrant advocates say crossings were already falling before Trump took office.

stories.title: Airlines Dig Out After the Longest Nationwide Ground Stop in 25 Years
paragraphs: More than 2,000 flights were canceled Saturday as airlines worked through the fallout from Friday's nationwide ground stop. AP reports officials blamed new technology that overloaded antiquated air traffic equipment. The stop lasted more than four hours and was lifted around 8:15 p.m. ET Friday.

CBS News reports Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said overloaded routers produced inconsistent data. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said there was no cyberattack and no link to the Microsoft outage. Duffy warned of more outages unless Congress funds new systems. He expects flights to be back up for Thanksgiving travel.

stories.title: All Aboard Survive After a Tanker Slams Into a New Orleans River Cruise Boat

photo.alt: Paddlewheel riverboat in New Orleans; file photo, 2026.

paragraphs: A tanker that apparently lost its steering hit the docked American Heritage river cruise boat in New Orleans on Friday. AP reports all 180 people aboard survived after the boat flipped and many plunged into the Mississippi River. The mayor said 32 people went to the hospital, none with critical injuries.

CBS News reports the Coast Guard is investigating an apparent loss of steering. NTSB investigators planned to drive to New Orleans because of the nationwide flight disruption. The tanker, Atlantic Asphalt, is owned by a subsidiary of China State Shipbuilding Corporation, according to MarineTraffic.

stories.title: Alaska Elects Its First Democratic Governor Since 1998
paragraphs: AP reports Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins won the Alaska governor race, the first Democrat elected to the office since 1998. He defeated three Republicans, including Trump-endorsed Bernadette Wilson. Democrats will now hold the governor's office in 30 states.

NBC News reports Kreiss-Tomkins won a majority on the first ballot, so ranked choice counting was not needed. At 37, he will be the youngest governor in Alaska history. He campaigned on school funding, lower energy costs and a pause on new data centers. He takes office Dec. 7.

deep_dive.title: Why States Can Wait Until July to Drop People Over Medicaid Work Rules

photo.alt: Doctor filling out a form; file photo, 2025.

paragraphs: What happened. The Trump administration told states Friday they can wait until July before removing people from Medicaid for missing a work requirement. CMS announced an optional hold harmless period through June 30, 2027. The requirement still takes effect nationally on Jan. 1. States using the delay must still check eligibility but cannot drop people solely for noncompliance.

Why it matters. KFF says the 2025 reconciliation law requires 44 states, including DC, to apply work rules to certain adults. Many enrollees must work, volunteer or join a work program 80 hours a month, or attend school half-time. AP reports critics say most affected enrollees already work and fear the paperwork. Exceptions cover people over 64 and parents of children under 14.

What each side says. CMS official Dan Brillman said states have made real progress and were clear about what it takes to get this right. Kathy Hempstead of the Robert Wood Johnson Foundation told AP the extra time should mean fewer people lose coverage over administrative failures. The National Association of Medicaid Directors said state leaders appreciate the added flexibility.

What comes next. It is not yet clear which states will use the extra time, AP reports. Democrats, who take control of both chambers of Congress in January, have said they want to roll back the requirements. A Boston federal court recently ruled that medically frail people should not be bound by the rules. CMS urges states to verify work through existing data first.

World view: ASEAN weighs Myanmar's return. Leaders meeting in Manila from Nov. 15 to 17 will review a five-year ban on Myanmar's military-backed leaders; Reuters reports.
Ten die in Guinea mining clashes. Violence with security forces broke out in a gold region after authorities banned artisanal mining in Siguiri on Nov. 2; Reuters reports.
China probes a former Wuhan chief. Wang Zhonglin, who led Hubei and Wuhan early in the COVID-19 pandemic, is under investigation, the anti-graft watchdog said; Reuters reports.
Belgium splits over shop cyberattacks. The interior minister said Iran was very likely behind them, while the foreign minister said evidence was insufficient; Reuters reports.
Need to know: The US reportedly loses measles-free status. The Pan American Health Organization ended the 26-year status, the Wall Street Journal reported; Reuters reports.
New York wins a highway funds case. An appeals court ruled the administration overstepped by withholding $73.5 million over commercial driver licenses; Reuters reports.
Lutnick agrees to testify. The commerce secretary will appear before the Senate Banking Committee on Dec. 10 over AI chip export oversight; CBS News reports.
Boebert loses her seat. Democrat Eileen Laubacher, a retired Navy rear admiral, narrowly defeated the Colorado Republican, US media projected; Reuters reports.
Money & markets: Stocks end Friday mixed. At Friday's close the Dow rose 0.10%, while the S&P 500 fell 0.40% and the Nasdaq slid 0.91%; Reuters reports.
The Fed flags AI as a top risk. In its financial stability survey, 87% of contacts cited AI as a risk, up from 50% in May; Reuters reports.
China and the US discuss trade. Their first trade council meeting covered tariff cuts and farm trade ahead of an expected Xi-Trump meeting next week; Reuters reports.
Nvidia and Anthropic face tests. Nvidia reports results Tuesday, and Anthropic's IPO could value the AI lab at up to $1.4 trillion; Reuters reports.
Future frontiers: Starship aims for a round trip. SpaceX launched its 15th flight Friday and planned to catch the upper stage at its Texas tower on Saturday; Reuters reports.
Scientists map a key brain region. A cellular atlas of the basal ganglia could help guide treatments for diseases such as Parkinson's and Huntington's; Reuters reports.
China adds two GLP-1 drugs to insurance. Pfizer's ecnoglutide and Innovent's mazdutide will be covered for type 2 diabetes from Jan. 1; Reuters reports.
The FDA shelves a fast-track program. A voucher plan meant to cut some drug reviews to one or two months was dropped, six sources said; Reuters reports.
The score: Svitolina upsets Sabalenka. She won 6-3 3-6 6-1 to reach the WTA Finals semifinals in Indian Wells, where she faces Linda Noskova; Reuters reports.
The Dutch rout Greece 7-0. Tijjani Reijnders scored a first-half hat-trick in the Nations League, while Germany beat Serbia 3-1; Reuters reports.
The Red Sox land Jake Bauers. The first baseman agreed to a four-year, $58 million deal, ESPN reported; Reuters reports.
Dejounte Murray seeks a trade. The Pelicans and the guard's agent are working to fulfill his request, ESPN reported; Reuters reports.
Life & culture: AI music gets an awards show. The first US AI Music Awards in Los Angeles gave top honors to Xania Monet, an AI-generated avatar; Reuters reports.
Stray Kids plan stadium shows. The K-pop group's tour opens a North American leg in Seattle on May 16, 2027; Reuters reports.
A brokerage's AI band draws views. Samsung Securities' AI-generated K-pop group LUMINA passed 3 million YouTube views about five weeks after its debut; Reuters reports.
Pope Leo returns to Chiclayo. A nearby Peruvian town hopes he will recognize a miracle residents believe occurred nearly four centuries ago; Reuters reports.

stories.title: Trump, Putin and Xi Plan a Three-Way Meeting in China
paragraphs: Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping plan to meet next week on the sidelines of the Apec summit in Shenzhen. The BBC reports that the White House says nuclear arms reduction will be among the topics. Iran may also be discussed, but not Ukraine. A senior U.S. official said no agreement was expected.

Reuters, citing the New York Post, reports that the trilateral summit will take place on Thursday. CNBC reports that Elon Musk will accompany Trump to the Apec summit on Nov. 18 and 19. Officials said Trump does not plan to raise the Nvidia spy allegations with Xi.

photo.alt: Shenzhen skyline at dusk, 2025 file photo

stories.title: UN Nuclear Watchdog Grows Concerned About an Uninspected Iranian Site
paragraphs: The International Atomic Energy Agency says it is increasingly concerned about an Iranian nuclear facility it has not inspected. The BBC reports that the IAEA does not know the plant’s exact location or whether it holds nuclear material. Iran told the agency about the Isfahan enrichment plant a day before Israel began strikes in June 2025.

The Guardian reports that the agency says Iran refuses to allow inspections of the Isfahan facility. That leaves the agency unable to verify Iran’s enriched uranium stockpile. Before the 2025 strikes, Iran held an estimated 441kg enriched to 60%, close to weapons grade. Iran denies seeking nuclear weapons and says its programme is peaceful.

photo.alt: Mosque dome in Isfahan, Iran, 2025 file photo

stories.title: Nvidia Scandal Puts Singapore’s Chip Hub Under Scrutiny
paragraphs: Nvidia founder Jensen Huang stepped down on Thursday after admitting an affair with a woman reportedly linked to Singapore firm Megaspeed. The BBC reports that Megaspeed became the biggest buyer of Nvidia chips in South East Asia. It is suspected of giving Chinese companies backdoor access to those chips. Singapore was Nvidia’s second-largest billing centre last year.

The BBC reports that Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent blamed the Commerce Department for weak oversight of AI chip exports. He said several agencies had wanted Megaspeed on the entity list for months. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has been called to testify before the Senate Banking Committee next month. Singapore says it expects firms to respect other countries’ export rules.

photo.alt: Singapore financial district at night, 2026 file photo

deep_dive.title: Hungary Finds Nearly $20 Million in Cash in a Former Minister's Graft Probe
paragraphs: What happened. Hungarian investigators have seized cash worth $19.5 million in a probe into a former minister under Viktor Orbán. The Guardian reports that the money was buried in forests and hidden in farm buildings, warehouses and homes. Some was kept in safes in secluded locations. The two-day search took place on Thursday and Friday.

The accused. Miklós Seszták served as national development minister from 2014 to 2018. The BBC reports that he is accused of taking bribes in a scheme involving the state transport company. The Guardian says the scheme involved buying secondhand buses at inflated prices. Seszták denies wrongdoing. The cash has been deposited into the state treasury.

A wider reckoning. Prime Minister Péter Magyar ousted Orbán in a landslide in April after promising an anti-corruption drive. He called the seizure the end of the Fidesz-KDNP mafia. The BBC reports that Orbán’s brother was detained on Monday in a people-smuggling case. Orbán called it political revenge and denies the corruption claims against his government.

Signs of change. The Guardian reports that Central European University is open to expanding in Budapest again. Pressure from Orbán’s government pushed its main activities to Vienna in 2019. The university has not held formal talks with the new government yet. Its interim rector said a bigger Budapest presence would symbolise academic freedom.
